login.note: Mostly third-party SSO — GitHub, Google, Apple, Forem Passport — plus email+password. The SSO buttons open the provider's own page, so the human finishes there and lands back on dev.to. No second factor of its own; whatever the provider enforces applies.

logout.note: GET /signout_confirm only renders the confirmation page. The real sign-out is a DELETE to /users/sign_out carrying the CSRF token (Devise is configured sign_out_via :delete), so a human clicks the confirm button — a plain GET of /users/sign_out will NOT end the session.

traps: The session cookies (_Forem_Session / remember_user_token) are HttpOnly — invisible to document.cookie, so a cookie check reports a live session as logged out.

/async_info/base_data answers HTTP 200 WHEN SIGNED OUT. The signed-out body is {broadcast, param, token} with no `user` key at all. The status code is not the verdict; the presence of `user` is. Same failure shape as reddit's me.json.
In that response `user` is a JSON STRING, not an object (the controller does user_data.to_json inside the JSON), so it needs a second JSON.parse before username exists.

dev.to is edge-cached and much of the page is hydrated client-side, so a probe that runs a fraction of a second too early can see body.dataset.user unset on a page that is genuinely signed in — that is why the fetch fallback exists and why it, not the dataset, is authoritative.

Anonymously fetched HTML always carries body[data-user-status="logged-out"] (confirmed here 2026-09-12), which is exactly what a cached page would also show. Never treat a scraped copy of the page as a session verdict.
notes: Probe strategy (a) then (b), and both were read out of Forem's own source rather than guessed. (a) body[data-user-status] is rendered by app/views/layouts/application.html.erb and is literally what Forem's own utilities/checkUserLoggedIn.js tests; body.dataset.user is the JSON record that utilities/userData.js parses. (b) is a credentialed same-origin GET of /async_info/base_data, the endpoint the app itself uses to hydrate the current user (app/controllers/async_info_controller.rb) — checked for the `user` FIELD because it returns 200 either way. Cookies are never consulted. UNVERIFIED: read off the upstream Forem repo (forem/forem@main) on 2026-09-12 but never executed against a live signed-in tab; dev.to runs its own fork, so the field names are the thing to confirm. A READ recipe has an easy path here: the public Forem API v1 at https://dev.to/api/articles?per_page=30 needs no session at all (send accept: application/vnd.forem.api-v1+json), and the PERSONALIZED feed is the session-cookie endpoint GET /api/feed (also /api/feed/:timeframe) — that pair, not DOM scraping, is where the next person should start.
probe_checked: 2026-09-14: Go client `auth` ran live against the owner profile and returned a clean signed_out verdict (base_data carries no user field). Signed-OUT path proven again; signed-IN path still a hypothesis (profile is not signed in here).
